headline: TEGNA close drives record revenue, debt surges to fund it
summary_short: Nexstar's Q1 FY2026 net revenue rose 13.1% y/y to $1,396M and net income attributable to the company grew 51.9% y/y to $164M, powered largely by the TEGNA acquisition that closed March 19, 2026; long-term debt nearly doubled to $12,152M to fund the deal.
summary_long: Record Q1 net revenue of $1,396M (+13.1% y/y) was driven by $106M of incremental TEGNA revenue plus legacy-unit growth in advertising ($548M, +19.1%, including a $35M political-ad lift) and distribution ($837M, +9.8%). Net income attributable rose 51.9% to $164M on TEGNA's contribution, a ~$47M deferred-tax benefit and political advertising, offset by $42M of one-time TEGNA costs and higher interest expense. Adjusted EBITDA reached $470M (+23.4%). Operating cash flow fell 14.2% to $289M on working-capital timing; Adjusted Free Cash Flow still grew 20.7% to $420M. The company financed the $3,657M TEGNA purchase with $9,381M of new debt, pushing total debt to $12,152M (net leverage 3.84x) while paying $56M in dividends. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: TEGNA acquisition added $106M incremental revenue; legacy units also grew advertising and distribution revenue.
TEGNA added $54M; legacy units saw higher rates, vMVPD subscriber growth and new CW affiliations, partly offset by MVPD subscriber attrition.
TEGNA added $51M; political advertising rose $35M to $41M in this election year; non-political advertising grew just 0.4%.
TEGNA-driven operating income growth, a roughly $47M deferred-tax revaluation benefit, and higher political ad revenue, partly offset by $42M of one-time TEGNA costs and higher interest expense.
TEGNA added $31M; legacy revenue growth and lower CW broadcast-rights amortization also contributed.
Higher net income was more than offset by working-capital timing and reduced cash distributions from the TVFN equity investment.
Higher Adjusted EBITDA, reduced CW broadcast-rights payments and lower capex, partly offset by lower TVFN distributions.
Financed the $3,657M TEGNA acquisition with $9,381M of new debt issuance, plus refinancing of existing credit facilities.
The TEGNA acquisition, closed March 19, 2026, is the dominant driver this quarter across revenue, taxes, cash flow and debt.
